summary.suggested: The Washington Post recalled famous fixed prize fights, including Tom Allen's losses on fouls to Joe Goss in Kentucky, where referee Eph Holland was said to be bought, and to Mike McCool.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Washington Post, Wednesday, December 9, 1896, page 8.

facts.fact: Allen fought Joe Goss in Kentucky; a sheriff and deputies broke up the fight and it moved to an adjoining county, where referee Eph Holland of Boston, said to be fixed, gave Goss the decision on a foul
Allen's backer Fred Watkins was said to have been swindled out of $1,000 by referee Eph Holland at the Goss fight
The paper claimed the referee called a foul against Allen in his fight with Mike McCool, and that McCool afterward acknowledged he was fairly beaten by Allen

notes: Retrospective written 1896 (Allen still alive, so not Legacy). The article gives no dates for the Goss and McCool fights; its account of the McCool fight ending in a foul is doubtful and may confuse fights.
